prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Phoenix. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Phoenix for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — but to give you the best, specific recommendations I’ll need one quick detail: what ZIP code or neighborhood in Phoenix are you closest to? Also tell me if you have dental insurance (and which plan), any medical issues (e.g., diabetes, osteoporosis, smoking), and whether you prefer an oral surgeon, periodontist, or prosthodontist (or don’t know).

While you reply, here’s a practical plan and the kinds of practices you should call — and why — so you can start right away.

Which specific types of practices to call (and why)
- Oral & Maxillofacial Surgeons (OMS)
  - Why: OMS specialists handle complex surgery, bone grafting, sinus lifts, IV sedation and medically complicated patients. Call if you expect extractions, bone augmentation, or sedation.
- Periodontists with implant practices
  - Why: Periodontists specialize in gums and implants; good when bone and soft-tissue health are a concern.
- Prosthodontists (or implant restorative dentists)
  - Why: They design and place the final implant crown/prosthesis and are best for esthetic or full-mouth reconstructions (All‑on‑4, fixed bridges).
- Multi‑disciplinary implant centers / large dental practices
  - Why: Often have OMS, periodontist, and prosthodontist in one location for coordinated care and single-case management.
- University or dental school clinics (e.g., dental teaching clinics)
  - Why: Lower cost supervised by faculty; good if budget is a concern.

What you should ask when you call (quick script)
- “Do you place dental implants? Which specialist would I see (OMS / periodontist / prosthodontist)?”
- “Do you do bone grafting or sinus lifts here?”
- “What implant systems do you use (Straumann, Nobel, Zimmer, Astra, etc.)?”
- “Will my treatment include a CBCT 3D scan in-office?”
- “Do you offer sedation (nitrous, oral conscious sedation, IV)?”
- “Do you handle the surgical placement and the restoration in-house or refer to another office?”
- “Can you provide an estimate (surgical fee, implant fixture, abutment, crown) and explain payment/financing?”
- “Do you accept my insurance or offer a treatment coordinator to check benefits?”

Key credentials and capabilities to prefer
- Board certification / memberships (AAOMS, American Academy of Periodontology, American College of Prosthodontists, AAID, ICOI)
- In‑office CBCT (3D imaging)
- On-site lab or strong lab partnerships for predictable restorations
- Experience with the specific case you need (single tooth, multiple teeth, All-on‑4)
- Good online reviews and before/after photos

Cost & timeframe expectations (so you know what to ask about)
- Typical single implant (placement + abutment + crown): varies widely; ask for itemized estimates. Bone grafting and sinus lifts add cost and healing time.
- Healing: 3–6 months if bone grafting; immediate/“same‑day” implant options exist for selected cases.
- Payment: most offices offer financing (CareCredit, in-office plans).

How I can help next
- If you give your ZIP or neighborhood and any insurance/preferences, I’ll compile 4–6 specific Phoenix‑area practices (phone, short reason to call each, what they specialize in) and help you prioritize which to call first.
